headline: Trump's Iran restraint sinks WTI 4.4% to $86.85; risk rebound lifts 2-year yield 5bp
summary: Oil and gasoline slumped to their lowest since late summer as Trump played down new strikes on Iran and talks showed progress, with WTI down $3.98 and RBOB down 4.5%. A 2.3% stock rebound drained the haven bid from Treasuries and a soft 3-year auction added pressure, lifting the 2-year about 5bp to near 4.57%, while gold rose about 1% on a weaker dollar and cheaper oil. Bunds edged up and the French 10-year hit a six-week low as Moody's held France's rating.
drivers: Iran de-escalation drains the oil war premium

Trump called new strikes on Iran highly unlikely while talks progress, and Iran reportedly agreed to negotiate on its nuclear programme. WTI settled -$3.98 at $86.85 and Brent -$5.75 at $92.57, then fell further after the settle.
Risk rebound and a soft 3-year auction lift the front end

The S&P 500 rose 2.3% and the VIX fell about 21%, removing last week's haven bid. The $58bn 3-year sale tailed 0.5bp at 4.627% with a 2.53 bid-to-cover, and the 2-year rose about 5bp to near 4.57% with December hike odds near 77–81%.
Weaker dollar and cheaper oil lift metals
The dollar index slipped about 0.4% toward 101.9 and lower oil eased inflation fears. Comex gold settled +$40.50 at $4,105 and spot reached about $4,140 late; silver settled +76¢ at $52.56.

Moody's left France's rating unchanged on Friday, and lower oil helped euro-area debt. The French 10-year fell about 2bp to near 4.73%, a six-week low, about 147bp over Bunds, while the Bund edged up about 1bp to 3.26%.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled -$3.98 (-4.4%) at $86.85, lowest since Aug 31, and slid to about $86 after the settle; Brent -$5.75 at $92.57.
oil.why: Trump said fresh strikes on Iran are highly unlikely while talks progress, and late reports said Iran agreed to negotiate on its nuclear programme, so traders cut the war premium again despite new attacks on ships near Hormuz. The physical market is soft: Dated Brent slipped to a discount to futures, OPEC output rose about 1.4m b/d in October, and JPMorgan puts the October surplus near 1.4m b/d.
oil.outlook: Bias lower in an $82–90 range while diplomacy holds and flows through Hormuz stay strong; $85 is the next support and a break opens the low $80s. A collapse in talks or a serious tanker attack that closes the strait would send WTI back above $90.
oil.watch: Iran talks, EIA STEO Tue Nov 10, OPEC report Wed Nov 11, EIA stocks Thu Nov 12 and the IEA report Fri Nov 13.

gas.note: Dec RBOB fell 12.58¢ (-4.5%) to $2.6509, the lowest settle since Mar 10; ULSD -2.7% to $4.2148.
gas.why: Gasoline tracked crude's slide as Iran de-escalation hopes cut the supply premium, and it fell more than diesel because winter-grade blends and post-season demand leave little seasonal support. The pump average is now catching down: AAA was near $4.01 on Monday, about 16¢ below a week ago, and GasBuddy already shows $3.96, the first sub-$4 reading since the summer.
gas.outlook: Bias lower in a $2.50–2.75 range as long as WTI holds below $90; retail prices should keep falling toward $3.85–3.90 over the next week or two. A crude rebound above $90 would push RBOB back toward $2.80.
gas.watch: Iran headlines, EIA gasoline stocks and refinery runs Thu Nov 12, and the AAA average crossing below $4.

gold.note: Comex Nov settled +$40.50 (+1.0%) at $4,105, the highest since Oct 21; spot near $4,140 late.
gold.why: Gold recovered Friday's loss because the dollar index fell about 0.4% toward 101.9 and the 4.4% oil drop eased inflation worries, which supports real returns on bullion. It rallied even though December Fed hike odds stayed high near 77–81% and stocks rebounded 2%, a sign that dip buyers remain active after last week's 4.6% gain. Prices pushed higher after the Comex settle.
gold.outlook: Range of about $4,080–4,200 with a mild upward tilt while the dollar softens; resistance is at $4,150 and $4,200, support at $4,070. A hot CPI that lifts hike odds above 85% would push it back toward $4,050.
gold.watch: US CPI Tue Nov 10, PPI Fri Nov 13, Fed speakers and the dollar.

silver.note: Comex Nov settled +76¢ (+1.5%) at $52.56, the highest since Oct 28; spot near $53.
silver.why: Silver outpaced gold as the weaker dollar, lower oil and a 2.7% Nasdaq rebound helped both its monetary and industrial sides. The chip-stock recovery matters most for silver because of solar and electronics demand, and short covering added to the move after its October low near $49. The gold/silver ratio eased to about 78.
silver.outlook: Range of about $51–55 with a mild upward tilt if tech stabilises; a close above $54 would open $55–56. A hot CPI or a fresh tech selloff would send it back toward $51.
silver.watch: US CPI Nov 10, chip-stock sentiment and China trade and inflation data.

us2y.note: Up about 5bp to near 4.57%, undoing part of last week's haven rally.
us2y.why: The 2-year led the selloff as a 2.3% stock rebound removed the safe-haven bid and traders rebuilt bets on Fed tightening after Friday's 165,000 payrolls beat; December hike odds stayed near 77–81%. The 3-year auction tailed 0.5bp at 4.627% with the weakest bid-to-cover since August 2025, as buyers balked after the six-week rally. Goolsbee said services inflation is picking up.
us2y.outlook: Bias modestly higher in a 4.50–4.65% range while a December hike looks likely; CPI decides the next move. A soft core print would pull it back toward 4.50%, while a hot one opens 4.65%.
us2y.watch: CPI Tue Nov 10, PPI Fri Nov 13 and Fed speakers before the Dec 8–9 meeting.

us5y.note: Up about 3bp to near 4.68% as the curve bear-flattened.
us5y.why: The belly rose with the front end because the tech rebound pulled money out of bonds and hike bets for 2026–27 were rebuilt. The weak 3-year auction, which drew record direct bidding but the lowest foreign share in fifteen months, also weighed on nearby maturities. Lower oil limited the rise by keeping inflation breakevens near multi-week lows.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.60–4.75% with a slight upward bias into CPI and refunding supply; a hot CPI targets 4.75%, while a soft one points back to 4.60%.
us5y.watch: CPI and the 10-year auction Nov 10, 30-year auction Nov 12.

us10y.note: Up about 1bp to near 4.87%; 2s10s flattened to about 30bp.
us10y.why: The 10-year rose far less than the 2-year because the 4.4% oil drop pulled inflation expectations lower even as the stock rebound cut haven demand. Investors also held back ahead of Tuesday's $42bn 10-year auction and the CPI report, and the NY Fed survey showed inflation expectations unchanged. With hikes back in focus, the curve keeps flattening.
us10y.outlook: Range of 4.80–4.95% with a flat bias; refunding supply and hike pricing cap rallies, while cheaper oil limits selloffs. A hot CPI or a weak 10-year auction would test 4.95%; a soft CPI brings 4.80% back.
us10y.watch: CPI and the 10-year auction Tue Nov 10, bond market closed Wed Nov 11 for Veterans Day.

us30y.note: Up about 1bp to near 5.27%, the smallest move on the curve.
us30y.why: The long bond barely moved because falling oil and a Fed seen ready to hike both support long-run inflation control, which flattens the curve. Treasury's dropping of 'at least' from its auction-size guidance has raised hopes of smaller 20- and 30-year sales next year. Still, Thursday's $25bn 30-year auction is keeping buyers cautious.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.18–5.35% with a flattening bias while hike pricing builds; a weak 30-year auction or an oil rebound would test 5.35%.
us30y.watch: CPI Nov 10 and the 30-year auction Thu Nov 12.

de2y.note: Edged up to near 3.00% after dipping to about 2.95% in the morning.
de2y.why: Schatz yields fell early with oil and lingering tech worries, then rose once stocks rallied and traders turned back to central bank pricing. Markets still expect the ECB to hike in December with euro-area inflation near 4.0%, and Friday's US payrolls beat keeps global front-end rates firm. The curve flattened as short yields rose most.
de2y.outlook: Range of 2.92–3.05% with a December ECB hike largely priced; Brent holding below $90 for a few weeks would be needed to unwind it. Bias flat.
de2y.watch: US CPI Nov 10, German final CPI Wed Nov 11, euro-area Q3 GDP Fri Nov 13 and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.07% as the morning rally faded.
de5y.why: The 5-year followed the same pattern as the 2-year: early gains on lower oil, then a reversal as European stocks rose about 1.3% and investors refocused on likely December hikes from both the Fed and the ECB. Cheaper oil limited the rise by trimming inflation expectations.
de5y.outlook: Range of 2.98–3.12% with no strong bias; a hot US CPI would push it toward 3.12%, while Brent near $90 points to 3.00%.
de5y.watch: US CPI Nov 10, German CPI Nov 11 and euro-area GDP Nov 13.

de10y.note: Up about 1bp to near 3.26% after trading 3.22–3.28%, still near the late-August lows.
de10y.why: Bunds rallied early as Brent fell, then turned lower in price as stocks rebounded and US yields rose, leaving the 10-year slightly higher on the day. The yield has fallen four weeks in a row on haven demand and lower oil, so the move looks like consolidation ahead of US CPI rather than a turn.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.20–3.32% with a slight downward bias while oil keeps falling; a hot US CPI or hawkish ECB talk would test 3.32%.
de10y.watch: US CPI Nov 10, German CPI Nov 11, euro-area GDP and Fitch's Germany review Nov 13.

de30y.note: Little changed near 3.63%, flatter against the short end.
de30y.why: The long end barely moved as lower oil offset the risk rebound, so the curve flattened with short yields rising more. Heavy German issuance to fund fiscal expansion keeps a premium in 30-year debt, which is why it lagged last week's rally.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.58–3.70% with a steepening bias over time; a break above 3.70% would need an oil spike or a hawkish ECB shift.
de30y.watch: German auctions, US CPI Nov 10 and the US 30-year auction Nov 12.

fr2y.note: Little changed near 3.48%, holding below the late-October levels.
fr2y.why: Short OATs mostly follow ECB pricing, so they tracked Schatz and ended flat as the morning oil-led rally faded. The Bank of France's estimate that the economy will grow moderately in the fourth quarter, avoiding recession after a 0.1% Q3 contraction, supports the hike case but eases credit worries.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.40–3.55% with a flat bias; a dovish ECB turn after a lasting oil drop is the main downside trigger.
fr2y.watch: French Q3 unemployment Tue Nov 10, French final CPI Fri Nov 13 and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Down about 1–2bp to near 4.09%, outperforming Bunds.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT gained as investors kept buying French debt after Moody's left the AA rating unchanged on Friday, though with a negative outlook. Lower oil also helps France more than Germany because energy feeds directly into its fiscal and growth outlook. The Senate debate on the 2027 budget remains the main risk.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.02–4.18% with a mild tightening bias versus Bunds; a setback in the Senate budget process would push it back toward 4.18%.
fr5y.watch: Senate budget debate, French CPI Nov 13 and rating reviews.

fr10y.note: Down about 2bp to near 4.73%, a six-week low; the spread to Bunds narrowed to about 147bp.
fr10y.why: OATs outperformed for a second session after Moody's held France's rating, removing a downgrade risk, and as cheaper oil eased deficit fears. The 10-year briefly rose to 4.80% in the morning before falling steadily. ING notes the spread is now well below the 175bp peak, though France still needs a lasting fiscal effort to avoid future downgrades.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.65–4.82% with the spread likely held at 140–155bp; a budget passed even by decree could tighten it toward 140bp, while a government crisis would push it back above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Senate budget debate, the Dec 9 Senate vote and rating reviews.

fr30y.note: Down about 1bp to near 5.26%, lagging shorter OATs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT edged lower with the rest of the French curve after Moody's decision, but gained less because long-dated French debt carries the most fiscal risk, with deficits near 5% of GDP and debt heading toward 122% of GDP in 2027. Global long-end supply this week also limited buying.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.18–5.38% with a bias to underperform shorter OATs; a credible budget deal could pull it toward 5.18%, while political escalation risks a retest of the highs.
fr30y.watch: French politics, Senate budget debate and OAT auctions.

watch: Next: US CPI, the 10-year auction and EIA STEO Tue Nov 10, US bond market closed and OPEC report Wed Nov 11, 30-year auction and EIA stocks Thu Nov 12, US PPI, euro-area GDP and the IEA report Fri Nov 13, then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
